RaMP multi-DB ORA (Reactome + SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways) returned two SMPDB pathways — Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182, FDR = 1.22 × 10⁻¹⁵) and Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043, FDR = 1.22 × 10⁻¹⁵) — as co-ranked hits at the top of the list, both enriched with five input metabolites (galactinol, sucrose, myo-inositol, galactitol, glycerol) and a fold-enrichment of 1 743–1 801. react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal centred on galactose metabolism and its downstream Leloir-pathway derivatives. RaMP multi-DB ORA (Reactome + SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways) returned two SMPDB pathways — Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182, FDR = 1.22 × 10⁻¹⁵) and Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043, FDR = 1.22 × 10⁻¹⁵) — as co-ranked hits at the top of the list, both enriched with five input metabolites (galactinol, sucrose, myo-inositol, galactitol, glycerol) and a fold-enrichment of 1 743–1 801. MetaboAnalystR's KEGG-specific PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00052 Galactose Metabolism as the top hit (p = 9.53 × 10⁻¹⁰) with the same five metabolites. The m/z-direct Mummichog algorithm, which operates on the empirical human_mfn network without direct ID lookups, placed galactose_metabolism at rank 3 (p = 8.40 × 10⁻⁴) and captured four of the five driver compounds (galactinol, sucrose, galactitol, glycerol) through mass-network proximity. Acetylcholine and myo-inositol additionally appear in the Mummichog glycerophospholipid metabolism and phosphatidylinositol phosphate metabolism modules, consistent with their roles as membrane-lipid precursors and osmolytes linked to galactose flux. The aflatoxin B1 exo-8,9-epoxide was detected as a co-hit within the Mummichog sialic-acid and hexose-phosphorylation networks, suggesting xenobiotic exposure co-occurs with perturbed sugar metabolism. The strong three-paradigm consensus on galactose metabolism (p < 10⁻⁹ across ORA tools, rank ≤ 3 in m/z-direct) and the presence of five Leloir-pathway intermediates (galactinol → sucrose → galactitol, with myo-inositol as a downstream cyclitol and glycerol as a downstream glycerol-backbone source) indicate that the treatment strongly dysregulates galactose catabolism, consistent with either galactose overload, galactosemia-like enzyme inhibition, or oxidative stress requiring myo-inositol as a protective osmolyte.
